item.title: China outlines sci-tech priorities for 2026-2030 to underpin high-quality development
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
BEIJING, Sept. 29 (Xinhua) -- China will strengthen basic research, tackle core technologies and speed up the industrial application of research results during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) to better support high-quality development, officials of the Ministry of Science and Technology said on Tuesday.
At a press conference held by the State Council Information Office, Minister of Science and Technology Yin Hejun said China's total R&D spending exceeded 3.92 trillion yuan (about 582 billion U.S. dollars) in 2025, or 2.8 percent of GDP. This amount exceeded the average among the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) members for the first time.
China has ranked first in the world for many consecutive years in international patent applications under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) and in papers published in high-level international journals, Yin said.
China ranks ninth among 60 countries in overall national innovation capability, according to the National Innovation Index Report 2025 released by the Chinese Academy of Science and Technology for Development.
Looking ahead, basic research will be organized in areas such as mathematical theory and applications, control of states of matter, synthetic biology, the materials genome, controlled nuclear fusion and intelligent scientist systems, Yin said.
He also called for faster application of artificial intelligence (AI) in scientific research to lead a shift in how research is carried out.
Paramount core technologies are another important priority, Yin said. China will push for progress along the entire innovation chain in key fields such as integrated circuits, machine tools and high-end instruments, and step up R&D in frontier technologies including AI, quantum technology, biotechnology and brain-computer interfaces.
Sci-tech innovation should also deliver more quality products and services that improve people's well-being, he said, with tasks laid out in areas including environmental pollution control, resource recycling, agricultural biological breeding, innovative drug development, high-end medical equipment and responses to population aging.
On turning research results into real-world productivity, Zhang Guangjun, vice minister of science and technology, said China will break the stereotype of producing results first and considering their application later on. Policies will instead direct research to where demand lies and ensure that results, once achieved, can be put to use, so that scientific and industrial innovation are planned in tandem and support one another, he said.
Zhang also called for stronger enterprise-led collaboration among industry, universities and research institutes, with innovation resources such as projects, platforms, data, talent and funding channeled to enterprises. Proof-of-concept and pilot-scale testing platforms will be built to help technologies mature and upgrade faster, he said.
Venture capital has played a vital role, with investors increasingly backing early-stage and small companies, taking a long-term view and focusing on hard technology, said Qiu Yong, vice minister of science and technology. New funds raised in the equity investment market exceeded 1 trillion yuan in the first half of 2026, up 49 percent year on year, he said, citing statistics from relevant institutions.
Universities are adjusting their disciplines to meet urgent national needs, he said.
China will continue to build Beijing and the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, Shanghai and the wider Yangtze River Delta, and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area into international sci-tech innovation centers, Yin said. The three centers account for 58.8 percent of the country's R&D spending and 81.1 percent of its PCT international patent applications, and are helping drive innovation in surrounding provinces and municipalities and across the country.
R&D spending in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region has reached 4.48 percent of regional GDP, with major sci-tech achievements emerging in fields such as AI and biomanufacturing, Yin said.
The Yangtze River Delta accounts for nearly 30 percent of the country's basic research spending, with corporate spending on basic research up 38.3 percent year on year in 2025. It has witnessed key breakthroughs in areas such as integrated circuits and quantum technology, he said.
The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area draws on Guangdong's industrial innovation strengths and the science and education resources of Hong Kong and Macao, Yin said. Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao have jointly built 35 laboratories, and produced 14,000 papers under international collaboration.

item.title: China's manufacturing PMI at 50.1 in September
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- The purchasing managers' index (PMI) for China's manufacturing sector stood at 50.1 in September 2026, up 0.3 percentage points from August and back to the expansion zone, official data showed on Wednesday.
A reading above 50 indicates expansion, while a reading below 50 signifies contraction.
The manufacturing sector's business climate improved further in September, with the PMI rising for a second consecutive month, said Huo Lihui, a chief statistician with the National Bureau of Statistics.
Among the 21 industries surveyed, 12 reported a PMI above the expansion threshold, four more than the previous month, Huo noted.
The sector saw expansion in both manufacturing output and market demand in September. The production sub-index climbed to 51.7, up 1.3 percentage points from August, while the new orders index was at 50.5, still above the threshold.
Driven by the acceleration in production, enterprises' willingness to purchase strengthened, with the procurement volume index reaching 51.0, an increase of 0.5 percentage points from the previous month, said Huo.
PMI for the equipment manufacturing industry, the high-tech manufacturing industry and the consumer goods industry stood at 51, 52.5 and 50.7, respectively, all remaining in the expansion zone.
Affected by rising international commodity prices and growing demand in some industries, the purchasing price index for major raw materials and the ex-factory price index for manufacturing stood at 60.8 and 54, respectively, up 4.2 percentage points and 3.6 percentage points from the previous month.
PMI for medium-sized and small manufacturing enterprises came in at 49.7 and 48.9, respectively, increases of 0.3 percentage points and 1 percentage point from the previous month, as business activity picked up.

item.title: China conducts military, law-enforcement patrols around Huangyan Dao
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese military and the China Coast Guard (CCG) conducted combat readiness patrols and law-enforcement patrols, respectively, around the country's Huangyan Dao on Wednesday.
Naval and air units of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Southern Theater Command conducted combat readiness patrols in the territorial sea and airspace of Huangyan Dao and its surrounding areas.
The theater command has organized its forces to carry out patrols in relevant areas since early September, the theater command said in a statement.
The patrols aim to further enhance control of relevant sea areas and airspace, and serve as an effective countermeasure to all sorts of rights violations and provocative acts, according to the statement.
Huangyan Dao is part of China's inherent territory. The Chinese military will resolutely safeguard China's sovereignty and security and firmly uphold peace and stability in the South China Sea, the statement added.
On the same day, the CCG conducted law-enforcement patrols in the territorial sea of the Huangyan Dao and its surrounding areas.
Law-enforcement patrols have been enhanced since early September, the CCG said, noting that its forces regulated ships engaged in illegal rights-violating activities in accordance with laws and regulations during the patrols.
The patrols are meant to further strengthen the orderly management of relevant waters and resolutely safeguard China's territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests, the CCG said.
China has sovereignty over Nanhai Zhudao (the South China Sea Islands), consisting of Dongsha Qundao (the Dongsha Islands), Xisha Qundao (the Xisha Islands), Zhongsha Qundao (the Zhongsha Islands) and Nansha Qundao (the Nansha Islands). Huangyan Dao is located in the Zhongsha Islands.
China has historic rights in the South China Sea. China also has internal waters, territorial sea, contiguous zone, exclusive economic zone and continental shelf, based on Nanhai Zhudao.
The international community has long widely recognized Nanhai Zhudao as part of China's territory.

item.title: Nishan Forum 2026: Experts on Confucianism and its relevance today
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
A ceremony commemorating Confucius is held at the Temple of Confucius in Qufu, east China's Shandong Province, September 28, 2026. /VCG
Over 2,500 years after the birth of Confucius in Nishan, the ancient wisdom of the land is still inspiring new conversations about the challenges facing humanity today.
The 12th Nishan Forum on World Civilizations opened on Monday under the theme "Civilization, Order and Justice," bringing together officials, scholars and cultural representatives from around the world to discuss the future of human civilization.
The forum focuses on the contemporary relevance of Confucianism, global governance, dialogue among civilizations and the role of AI in shaping humanity's future.
František Škvrnda, an assistant professor at the Bratislava University of Economics and Business in Slovakia, said Confucianism is a rich and diverse intellectual tradition that covers almost every major field of humanities and social sciences. He highlighted the value of comparing the philosophies of Confucius and Socrates, stressing that exchanges between civilizations are key to human progress.
"Exploring the links between ancient Chinese and Greek wisdom can deepen mutual understanding and cooperation between Eastern and Western civilizations," he said, adding that it lays the foundation for broader cooperation in social, economic and political affairs.
Confucian wisdom for today's world
Against the backdrop of growing differences and conflicts between civilizations, Škvrnda said Confucianism offers universal values that remain relevant to today's world. He was particularly fascinated by its ability to address fundamental and enduring questions of humanity and offer ideas for tackling contemporary challenges.
He said Confucianism emphasizes values such as benevolence, compassion and helping those in need. It also calls for improving people's living conditions and building a well-governed society that protects livelihoods and enables people to live with dignity.
Škvrnda said Confucianism offers insights into challenges such as inequality, conflicts between countries and environmental crises, while its values of social harmony, justice, peace and respect for life and nature could contribute to a new philosophy of coexistence and the building of a community with a shared future for humanity.
Meanwhile, Confucian ideas also bring a distinct perspective to international relations.
Eduardo Daniel Oviedo, a professor at the School of Political Science and International Relations at the National University of Rosario in Argentina, said the forum's theme of "Civilization, Order and Justice" is closely linked to the impact of civilizations on the international system and global order. "Civilizations influence political order, while political order is shaped by law and, indirectly, by ideas of justice," he said.
Oviedo noted that Confucianism offers important insights into international relations, particularly its concept of "harmony" as a way to manage conflicts of interest between countries. He said harmony is closely linked to balance, including the balance of power, which can help promote peace among states.
Human values and AI governance
As AI develops rapidly, how to strike a balance between technological progress and human values has become an important issue. Traditional cultures and dialogue among civilizations may offer new perspectives on how technology can serve humanity.
Oviedo said the Confucian ideal of "Great Unity" could provide an ethical framework for AI based on the common good, responsibility, inclusiveness and coordination. The idea can make an important contribution to discussions on technology ethics, while a global framework for AI governance should also take into account the interests and aspirations of different countries, he said.
Škvrnda also agreed that drawing on the wisdom of classical civilizations can help guide the development of AI. He said Confucian ethical principles, together with sound economic planning and responsible social policies, could help turn AI into a transformative tool for advancing human civilization.

item.title: Xi pays tribute to national heroes on Martyrs' Day
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and other Party and state leaders attended a ceremony to present flower baskets to fallen national heroes at Tian'anmen Square in central Beijing on Wednesday morning.
The event was held to mark Martyrs' Day. Observed on Sept. 30, one day before National Day, the day commemorates those who gave their lives for national independence and prosperity.
Since Martyrs' Day was established in 2014, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, has maintained the tradition of paying homage to fallen heroes on the day.
The other leaders who attended the ceremony on Wednesday included Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng. They were joined by representatives from all walks of life.
At 10 a.m., all attendees sang the national anthem, followed by a moment of silence in tribute to the heroes who sacrificed their lives for the liberation of the Chinese people and the development of the People's Republic of China.
Nine large flower baskets were placed in front of the Monument to the People's Heroes.
Xi and other leaders walked up to the foot of the monument, where he straightened the ribbons on the baskets. Then, they walked around the monument to pay their tributes.
The baskets, with ribbons reading "Eternal Glory to the People's Heroes," were presented in the name of the CPC Central Committee; the National People's Congress Standing Committee; the State Council; the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference; the Central Military Commission; non-Communist parties, the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce, and patriots without party affiliations; people's organizations and people from all walks of life; veterans, retired senior officials and the relatives of martyrs; and Chinese Young Pioneers.
Yin Li, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and secretary of the CPC Beijing Municipal Committee, presided over the ceremony.
This year marks the 105th founding anniversary of the CPC and the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March, which lasted from 1934 to 1936. The arduous journey helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution.
